text:
Seeing lots of these types of posts.  And I agree, life is obviously much more expensive these days.

But I'm wondering if anyone has done a study comparing what people were buying week in and out in the 70's and 80's versus today?  

I remember growing up, I got to buy 2 things of any value each year!  My birthday and Christmas.  That was it, and it wasn't a massive item either.   Maybe got a little pocket money, but I had to work a high-school job to have anything.  The TV was swapped out every 10 yrs. A holiday was a road trip.  Clothes were looked after, some passed down. A restaurant was maybe once a month and a bagged lunch to school/work.  And even with this, there wasn't much money left over. It was no picnic.

Today, families (including mine) seem to buy all sorts of shit daily. The money flows like water.  Coffees daily, order in 2-4 times weekly, restaurants and cocktails,  5 streaming plans, phones for all, flat-screen every room, to lazy to mow own grass, uber everywhere, one car per adult, clothes swapped frequently, renovations often, international trips, etc etc 

So when we talk about housing affordability, how much of this is choice/preference?
